# API reference

## The C ABI

The headers in `sdk/include/shard` are the contract between a plugin and the engine. This page is generated from their comments, in reading order. See [Plugins](concepts/plugins.md#the-c-abi-and-the-sdk) for the concepts and [the tutorial](tutorials/write-a-game-with-the-sdk.md) to build a plugin.

Every function says which thread may call it : `any`, `system` (from inside a system, possibly in parallel with others), `script` (from a script callback) or `main` (the main thread, outside systems). A function returns a `ShardResult`, either `SHARD_OK` (0) or a negative error, and the details go to the engine's log under the plugin's id. Strings are `ShardStr` : UTF-8, not necessarily zero terminated, valid for the duration of the call. A "text out" function takes `(buffer, capacity, *size)`, copies what fits and returns the full length.

### shard_abi.h

Shard C ABI : base types, versions and rules. Compiles as C11 and as C++17.

These headers ARE the ABI (see `docs/design-notes/c-abi-sdk.fr.md`, section 3). The rules :

* plain C : no classes, references, overloads or `enum class`; no `int`, `long`, `bool` or `size_t` inside a struct
* every struct that crosses the boundary starts with `uint32_t structSize`; fields are only ever added at the END
* the host never keeps a pointer it was handed unless the doc of that function says so
* no exception crosses the boundary; failures are a `ShardResult`

Changing a struct without bumping `SHARD_ABI_MINOR` is a bug : `tests/plugins/abi_layout_tests.cpp` pins every layout.

| | Value | |
|---|---|---|
| `SHARD_ABI_MAJOR` | `1` |  |
| `SHARD_ABI_MINOR` | `6` |  |

Calling convention of every function pointer in the tables. Empty on `x86_64` and arm64.

| | Value | |
|---|---|---|
| `SHARD_CALL` |  |  |
| `SHARD_PLUGIN_EXPORT` | depends on the platform |  |

**Results**

```c
typedef int32_t ShardResult;
```

| `SHARD_E_INVALID_ARG` | `(-1)` |  |
| `SHARD_E_NOT_FOUND` | `(-2)` |  |
| `SHARD_E_ALREADY_EXISTS` | `(-3)` |  |
| `SHARD_E_WRONG_THREAD` | `(-4)` |  |
| `SHARD_E_STALE_HANDLE` | `(-5)` |  |
| `SHARD_E_UNSUPPORTED` | `(-6)` |  |
| `SHARD_E_OUT_OF_MEMORY` | `(-7)` |  |
| `SHARD_E_INTERNAL` | `(-8)` |  |
| `SHARD_FALSE` | `0` |  |
| `SHARD_TRUE` | `1` |  |

#### ShardStr

**Strings**

UTF-8, not necessarily zero terminated. A string received through a call is valid for that call only : keeping it means copying it.

```c
const char* data;
uint64_t size;
```

**Handles**

Never a pointer to a host object. index + generation, so a stale one fails instead of reading freed memory. 0 is never valid.

```c
typedef uint64_t ShardPluginCtx;    // designates a plugin to the host
typedef uint64_t ShardState;    // the reload state being written or read : valid during on_prepare_reload / on_restore only (shard_state.h)
```

**Log levels**

| | Value | |
|---|---|---|
| `SHARD_LOG_INFO` | `0` |  |
| `SHARD_LOG_WARNING` | `1` |  |
| `SHARD_LOG_ERROR` | `2` |  |

### shard_host.h

Shard C ABI : what a plugin exports and what the host gives it.

#### ShardHostApi

**The host's table**

One static table for every plugin; a plugin designates itself with the `ShardPluginCtx` it is handed in each callback. The base is only what is needed to start; everything else is an interface fetched with `query_interface`, so this table barely grows.

```c
uint32_t structSize;
uint32_t abiMajor, abiMinor;
ShardStr engineVersion;    // "0.9.2", informative
```

thread : any

```c
void log(ShardPluginCtx ctx, uint32_t level, ShardStr message);
```

Memory counted against the plugin's budget (manifest budgets.memoryMB). Returns NULL on failure. What is allocated here is freed with `free` here : never with the plugin's own allocator, and never by the host's.

```c
void* alloc(ShardPluginCtx ctx, uint64_t size, uint64_t align);
void free(ShardPluginCtx ctx, void* p);
```

Looks an interface up by id (`"shard.plugin"`). `major` must match; the interface must be at least `minMinor`. On success `*out` points to a struct that starts with `uint32_t structSize`, valid until the host exits. `SHARD_E_NOT_FOUND` : the id is unknown, or this host does not offer it (an offline tool has no `"shard.systems"`).

```c
ShardResult query_interface(ShardStr id, uint32_t major, uint32_t minMinor, const void** out);
```

#### ShardWorldInfo

A world a module is told about. `name` is valid for the call.

```c
uint32_t structSize;
int32_t assetId;    // the world's asset id in the project, -1 if it has none
ShardStr name;
```

#### ShardPluginCallbacks

**The plugin's callbacks**

Same order and meaning as IPlugin. A callback returns `SHARD_OK`, or an error that makes the host fail the plugin (and the plugins that depend on it) with the message the plugin logged. Every callback is optional : NULL means `"nothing to do"`. All of them run on the main thread.

```c
uint32_t structSize;
ShardResult on_load(void* user, ShardPluginCtx ctx);
ShardResult on_initialize(void* user, ShardPluginCtx ctx);
ShardResult on_enable(void* user, ShardPluginCtx ctx);
ShardResult on_disable(void* user, ShardPluginCtx ctx);
ShardResult on_unload(void* user, ShardPluginCtx ctx);
```

Hot reload (`shard_state.h`). `on_prepare_reload` writes what must survive into `state` and returns `SHARD_OK` ; any other result (or no callback) makes the plugin not reloadable. `on_restore` reads it back in the new binary, after `on_enable`.

```c
ShardResult on_prepare_reload(void* user, ShardPluginCtx ctx, ShardState state);
ShardResult on_restore(void* user, ShardPluginCtx ctx, ShardState state);
```

Start and end of every frame while the plugin is enabled. Keep them short : their time is billed to the plugin.

```c
ShardResult on_frame_begin(void* user, ShardPluginCtx ctx, uint64_t frame);
ShardResult on_frame_end(void* user, ShardPluginCtx ctx, uint64_t frame);
```

Modules : the content folder is mounted (`mod://<id>/` is readable, `shard_content.h`), and what happens to the worlds

```c
ShardResult on_content_mounted(void* user, ShardPluginCtx ctx);
ShardResult on_world_loaded(void* user, ShardPluginCtx ctx, const ShardWorldInfo* world);
ShardResult on_world_unloaded(void* user, ShardPluginCtx ctx, const ShardWorldInfo* world);
ShardResult on_play_start(void* user, ShardPluginCtx ctx, const ShardWorldInfo* world);
ShardResult on_play_stop(void* user, ShardPluginCtx ctx, const ShardWorldInfo* world);
```

Offline tools : the tool is about to run `task` (`"cook"`, `"bake"`, `"validate"`) on the project file `project`. `SHARD_OK` lets it run ; anything else cancels it, with `*message` (copied before the call returns) as the reason. Unlike the others, an error here does not fail the plugin.

```c
ShardResult on_tool_task(void* user, ShardPluginCtx ctx, ShardStr task, ShardStr project, ShardStr* message);
```

Callbacks of later ABI revisions go HERE : the host checks structSize before reading them.

#### ShardPluginInfo

What the plugin fills in its entry point

```c
uint32_t structSize;    // the plugin sets it to sizeof(ShardPluginInfo) of the headers it was built with ; the host reads no field past it
uint32_t abiMajor, abiMinor;    // the plugin sets them to SHARD_ABI_MAJOR / SHARD_ABI_MINOR
ShardStr id;    // informative : the manifest is what the host trusts
void* user;    // handed back to every callback
const ShardPluginCallbacks* callbacks;    // must stay valid until on_unload returned
```

The entry point of an ABI `"c1"` plugin (manifest `"abi"`: `"c1"`). Called once, right after the library is loaded, on the main thread. `out` is zeroed. Return `SHARD_OK`, or an error to refuse to load.

```c
typedef ShardResult (*ShardPluginEntryFn)(const ShardHostApi* host, ShardPluginInfo* out);
```

| | Value | |
|---|---|---|
| `SHARD_PLUGIN_ENTRY_NAME` | `"shard_plugin_entry"` |  |

```c
SHARD_PLUGIN_EXPORT ShardResult shard_plugin_entry(const ShardHostApi* host, ShardPluginInfo* out);
```

### shard_plugin.h

Interface `"shard.plugin"` 1.2 : who the plugin is, as the host read it from the manifest, and where it runs. Thread : any. 1.1 added host and `has_permission` : ask for minor 1 (`query_interface`(`SHARD_IFACE_PLUGIN`, 1, 1, ...)) to call them. 1.2 added `random_stream` : ask for minor 2.

| | Value | |
|---|---|---|
| `SHARD_IFACE_PLUGIN` | `"shard.plugin"` |  |

#### ShardRandomState

The state of a PCG32 generator (O'Neill 2014) : `state` and `increment` are the two words of Shard's Random class. Whoever holds them continues the sequence with the same code and gets the same numbers on every platform (`shard/cpp/random.hpp` does).

```c
uint64_t state;
uint64_t increment;
```

#### ShardPluginApi

```c
uint32_t structSize;
```

The returned strings stay valid until the plugin is unloaded.

```c
ShardStr id(ShardPluginCtx ctx);    // "com.acme.weather"
ShardStr version(ShardPluginCtx ctx);    // "1.4.2"
ShardStr directory(ShardPluginCtx ctx);    // the plugin's folder, absolute, '/' separators
```

**1.1**

The executable the plugin runs in : `"editor"`, `"player"`, `"headless"` or `"tool"`

```c
ShardStr host(ShardPluginCtx ctx);
```

`SHARD_TRUE` if the manifest asks for that permission (`"fs.read:content"`, `"net"`...)

```c
int32_t has_permission(ShardPluginCtx ctx, ShardStr permission);
```

**1.2**

A generator for the stream `name` : derived from the run's seed, the plugin's id and the name, so the same name gives the same sequence in a replay of the run, and two plugins never share a stream. Name a stream after what draws from it (an actor's name and the script's), not after the order things started in. The generator is the caller's afterwards : no further call is needed.

```c
ShardResult random_stream(ShardPluginCtx ctx, ShardStr name, ShardRandomState* out);
```

### shard_cvars.h

Interface `"shard.cvars"` 1.0 : variables the plugin owns, readable from the console and the config files like the engine's own. A variable is named `"<plugin id>.<name>"` by the host. It lives until the plugin is disabled or unloaded ; after that its handle is stale (`SHARD_E_STALE_HANDLE`). The plugin changes its own variables with `set_*` (that bypasses the config layers and the read-only flag, as the owner) ; the console and the config files change them from outside. Numeric values are clamped to [min, max].

| | Value | |
|---|---|---|
| `SHARD_IFACE_CVARS` | `"shard.cvars"` |  |
| `SHARD_CVAR_READONLY` | `1u` | the console and the config files cannot change it |

```c
typedef uint64_t ShardCVar;    // generation << 32 | slot ; 0 is never valid
```

#### ShardCVarsApi

```c
uint32_t structSize;
```

thread : main. `SHARD_E_ALREADY_EXISTS` if the name is taken.

```c
ShardResult create_bool(ShardPluginCtx ctx, ShardStr name, int32_t value, ShardStr help, uint32_t flags, ShardCVar* out);
ShardResult create_int(ShardPluginCtx ctx, ShardStr name, int32_t value, ShardStr help, uint32_t flags, int32_t min, int32_t max, ShardCVar* out);
ShardResult create_float(ShardPluginCtx ctx, ShardStr name, float value, ShardStr help, uint32_t flags, float min, float max, ShardCVar* out);
ShardResult create_string(ShardPluginCtx ctx, ShardStr name, ShardStr value, ShardStr help, uint32_t flags, ShardCVar* out);
```

thread : any. `SHARD_E_INVALID_ARG` if the variable is of another type.

```c
ShardResult get_bool(ShardPluginCtx ctx, ShardCVar cvar, int32_t* out);
ShardResult get_int(ShardPluginCtx ctx, ShardCVar cvar, int32_t* out);
ShardResult get_float(ShardPluginCtx ctx, ShardCVar cvar, float* out);
```

Copies at most `capacity` bytes (no zero terminator) into `buffer` and stores the full length in `*size` : a value longer than the buffer is cut, and the caller can call again with a bigger one. `buffer` may be NULL to ask for the length.

```c
ShardResult get_string(ShardPluginCtx ctx, ShardCVar cvar, char* buffer, uint64_t capacity, uint64_t* size);
```

thread : main

```c
ShardResult set_bool(ShardPluginCtx ctx, ShardCVar cvar, int32_t value);
ShardResult set_int(ShardPluginCtx ctx, ShardCVar cvar, int32_t value);
ShardResult set_float(ShardPluginCtx ctx, ShardCVar cvar, float value);
ShardResult set_string(ShardPluginCtx ctx, ShardCVar cvar, ShardStr value);
```

### shard_commands.h

Interface `"shard.commands"` 1.0 : console commands. The command is removed with the plugin (disable or unload).

| | Value | |
|---|---|---|
| `SHARD_IFACE_COMMANDS` | `"shard.commands"` |  |

Runs the command. `args` are the words after the command name (`argCount` of them, valid for the call). The callback may point `*output` to a text to show the user (it is copied before the callback's caller returns : a static buffer or the plugin's own will do). Return `SHARD_OK` for success ; anything else is shown as a failure, with the output as the message. thread : main

```c
typedef ShardResult (*ShardCommandFn)(void* user, ShardPluginCtx ctx, const ShardStr* args, uint32_t argCount, ShardStr* output);
```

#### ShardCommandsApi

```c
uint32_t structSize;
```

The name is used as given : prefix it with your own (`"weather.set"`). `SHARD_E_ALREADY_EXISTS` if this plugin already added that name (case does not matter). A name another plugin or the engine already uses is replaced for as long as this plugin lives : the prefix is what keeps commands apart. thread : main

```c
ShardResult add(ShardPluginCtx ctx, ShardStr name, ShardStr help, ShardCommandFn run, void* user);
```

### shard_components.h

Interface `"shard.components"` 1.3 : component types described field by field.

One registration gives a type two faces, under one name (`"<plugin id>.<name>"`, made by the host) :

* an ECS component : a block of `size` bytes on an entity, what systems query and write (`shard_ecs.h`). Plain data : copied with memcpy,
```
never constructed nor destroyed, so no pointer to memory the plugin owns. What does not fit in the block goes in a blob (1.1, below) ;
```

* an actor component : what a world file saves, the editor shows in its inspector and an actor carries. Its fields are the ones described
```
here, read and written at their offset in the block.
```

An actor that has the actor component has the ECS component on its entity, with the same values : the actor component writes its values to the entity when it is loaded, edited or attached, and reads them back from the entity when the world is saved or copied. So what a system changed is what gets saved. An entity a plugin spawned on its own (`shard_ecs.h`, `cmd_spawn`) has no actor : it is not saved.

The type lives as long as the plugin is enabled. Its ECS id stays reserved for the whole run : a plugin enabled again gets the same `ShardComponentType` back, provided it describes the same size (a type whose size changed needs a restart of the engine).

Blobs (1.1) : bytes the host keeps outside the block, as many as needed (a chunk of voxels), counted against the plugin's memory budget. A field `SHARD_FIELD_BLOB` holds the `ShardBlob` handle. The plugin owns its blobs : `blob_free` gives one back, and all of them go with the plugin (disable, unload). The block is still copied with memcpy, so two blocks may hold the same handle : that is a shared blob, not a copy. The actor component is the exception, it owns the blobs of its blob fields : it saves their bytes with the world (base64), a copy of the actor (play mode) gets copies of them, and removing the component frees them. A system that puts a new blob in such a field frees the one it replaces.

Text and assets (1.2) : a field `SHARD_FIELD_STRING` holds a `ShardBlob` too, whose bytes are the UTF-8 text (no terminator) : the actor component owns it like any blob, but the inspector shows it as a text box and the world file saves it as a JSON string. `string_set` and `string_get` read and write it without touching the blob by hand. A field `SHARD_FIELD_ASSET` is an `int32_t`, the id of an asset of the project (0 : none) : the inspector shows an asset picker, the world file saves the asset by its name, and the engine knows the component uses it.

| | Value | |
|---|---|---|
| `SHARD_IFACE_COMPONENTS` | `"shard.components"` |  |

```c
typedef uint64_t ShardComponentType;    // 0 is never valid
typedef uint64_t ShardBlob;    // 0 is never valid : an empty blob field
```

Field types : the C type the field has in the block, and how it is saved

| | Value | |

| `SHARD_FIELD_F64` | `2u` | double |
| `SHARD_FIELD_I32` | `3u` | `int32_t` |
| `SHARD_FIELD_U32` | `4u` | `uint32_t` |
| `SHARD_FIELD_I64` | `5u` | `int64_t` |

| `SHARD_FIELD_BOOL` | `7u` | `uint8_t`, 0 or 1 |
| `SHARD_FIELD_VEC2` | `8u` | float[2] |

Field flags. Without any, a field is saved and editable in the inspector.

| | Value | |
|---|---|---|

```c
* by the script's text_get and text_set callbacks (shard_scripts.h) instead of a blob (1.5) */ typedef struct ShardFieldDesc { uint32_t structSize;
uint32_t type;    // SHARD_FIELD_*
ShardStr name;    // letters, digits and '_' ; "type", "active" and "tags" are reserved
uint32_t offset;    // in the block, aligned for its type
uint32_t flags;    // SHARD_FIELD_RUNTIME...
float min, max;    // bounds of the inspector's widget ; min == max : none
```

```c
uint32_t structSize;
```

Registers a type, from `on_load`. thread : main. `SHARD_E_INVALID_ARG` : a field out of the block, misaligned, overlapping another, of an unknown type, a bad name, a size or an alignment out of bounds (the log says which). `SHARD_E_ALREADY_EXISTS` : the name is taken (by this plugin, or by a type of another size).

```c
ShardResult register_type(ShardPluginCtx ctx, const ShardComponentDesc* desc, ShardComponentType* out);
```

The type of that full name (`"com.acme.weather.Cloud"`) : one of a C plugin, or one of the engine's that `shard_ecs.h` documents (`"shard.LocalTransform"`...). thread : any. `SHARD_E_NOT_FOUND` if there is none.

```c
ShardResult find_type(ShardPluginCtx ctx, ShardStr name, ShardComponentType* out);
```

Size and alignment of the block. thread : any

```c
ShardResult type_layout(ShardPluginCtx ctx, ShardComponentType type, uint32_t* size, uint32_t* align);
```

The fields of a type a C plugin registered (another plugin's, to read its blocks without its header). `out->structSize` must be set by the caller ; the strings in `*out` stay valid while that type is registered. thread : any. `SHARD_E_NOT_FOUND` : no such field / index.

```c
ShardResult field_count(ShardPluginCtx ctx, ShardComponentType type, uint32_t* count);
ShardResult field_at(ShardPluginCtx ctx, ShardComponentType type, uint32_t index, ShardFieldDesc* out);

```

**1.1 : blobs**

A blob of `size` bytes, zeroed (size may be 0). thread : any. `SHARD_E_OUT_OF_MEMORY` : over the plugin's enforced budget.

```c
ShardResult blob_create(ShardPluginCtx ctx, uint64_t size, ShardBlob* out);
```

Its bytes and size. The pointer stays valid until the blob is resized or freed ; reading and writing them from several threads at once is the plugin's to order (a system that writes a blob declares the component that holds it in its writes). thread : any. `SHARD_E_STALE_HANDLE` : freed, or not this plugin's.

```c
ShardResult blob_data(ShardPluginCtx ctx, ShardBlob blob, void** data, uint64_t* size);
```

New size, the first bytes kept, the rest zeroed ; the bytes move. thread : any

```c
ShardResult blob_resize(ShardPluginCtx ctx, ShardBlob blob, uint64_t size);
ShardResult blob_free(ShardPluginCtx ctx, ShardBlob blob);
```

Puts `text` (copied now) in the string field `*field` points to : in its blob if it holds a live one, else in a new blob whose handle is stored in `*field`. thread : any. `SHARD_E_OUT_OF_MEMORY` : over the plugin's enforced budget.

```c
ShardResult string_set(ShardPluginCtx ctx, ShardBlob* field, ShardStr text);
```

The text of a string field (empty for blob 0). `out->data` stays valid until the field is set again or freed. thread : any. `SHARD_E_STALE_HANDLE` : freed, or not this plugin's.

```c

```

### shard_ecs.h

Interface `"shard.ecs"` 1.1 : entities and their components, from inside a system (`shard_systems.h`).

Every function takes the `ShardEcs` the system was handed in its `ShardSystemCtx` : it is valid during that run, on that thread, and nowhere else (`SHARD_E_STALE_HANDLE`). A system reads and writes only the types it declared (reads / writes of its `ShardSystemDesc`, `SHARD_E_INVALID_ARG` otherwise ; an exclusive system may touch anything) : the scheduler relies on these declarations to run systems in parallel, and the result of a frame must not depend on it.

Structural changes (spawn, destroy, add, remove, `set_parent`) are recorded and applied at the end of the phase, system by system in registration order. spawn returns a placeholder that the later commands of the same run can use ; it means nothing afterwards. Changing the VALUE of a component (through the pointers of `each_chunk` and get) is immediate.

Moving an actor (1.1) : the engine's own components below are not written through these pointers, the actor's Transform is what drives them. `set_local_transform` records the new pose ; at the end of the phase the actor's Transform takes it (so does everything that follows a Transform : children, physics, the renderer) and the LocalTransform of the entity then holds it.

| | Value | |
|---|---|---|
| `SHARD_IFACE_ECS` | `"shard.ecs"` |  |

```c
typedef uint64_t ShardEntity;    // generation << 32 | index ; 0 is the null entity
typedef uint64_t ShardEcs;    // the registry as one system run sees it
```

#### ShardQuery

```c
uint32_t structSize;
uint32_t withCount;
uint32_t withoutCount;
const ShardComponentType* with;    // the entities have all of these ; the chunk's columns come in this order
const ShardComponentType* without;    // and none of these
```

#### ShardChunk

`count` entities that have the same components. columns[i] holds `count` blocks of query.with[i], one after the other : block j is at (char\*)columns[i] + j \* size of that type. Valid during the callback only.

```c
uint32_t structSize;
uint32_t count;
const ShardEntity* entities;
void* const* columns;
```

Return `SHARD_OK` to go on ; anything else stops the iteration and is what `each_chunk` returns.

```c
typedef ShardResult (*ShardChunkFn)(void* user, const ShardChunk* chunk);
```

#### ShardLocalTransform

`"shard.LocalTransform"` (`find_type`) : on the entity of every actor, its Transform relative to its parent. Read it ; move the actor with `set_local_transform` (1.1)

```c
float position[3];
float rotation[4];    // quaternion x, y, z, w
float scale[3];
```

#### ShardEcsApi

```c
uint32_t structSize;
```

Calls fn once per chunk of matching entities, in a stable order. No structural change happens meanwhile. thread : system

```c
ShardResult each_chunk(ShardEcs ecs, const ShardQuery* query, ShardChunkFn fn, void* user);
```

How many entities match. thread : system

```c
ShardResult count(ShardEcs ecs, const ShardQuery* query, uint64_t* out);
```

`SHARD_TRUE` if the entity exists (a placeholder of spawn does not, yet). thread : system

```c
int32_t is_alive(ShardEcs ecs, ShardEntity entity);
```

The entity's block of `type`, valid until the end of the run. `SHARD_E_NOT_FOUND` : it has none (or is dead). thread : system

```c
ShardResult get(ShardEcs ecs, ShardEntity entity, ShardComponentType type, void** out);
```

The parent (the null entity for a root). thread : system

```c
ShardResult parent(ShardEcs ecs, ShardEntity entity, ShardEntity* out);
```

Recorded, applied at the end of the phase. thread : system

```c
ShardResult spawn(ShardEcs ecs, ShardEntity* placeholder);
ShardResult destroy(ShardEcs ecs, ShardEntity entity);    // and its descendants
```

Adds the component, or overwrites its value. `size` must be the size of the type ; `data` is copied now.

```c
ShardResult add(ShardEcs ecs, ShardEntity entity, ShardComponentType type, const void* data, uint64_t size);
ShardResult remove(ShardEcs ecs, ShardEntity entity, ShardComponentType type);
ShardResult set_parent(ShardEcs ecs, ShardEntity child, ShardEntity parent);    // null parent : detach
```

**1.1 : moving actors**

Records the new local pose (relative to the parent) of the actor that stands behind `entity`. Applied at the end of the phase, on the main thread, after the structural changes ; when several systems set the same entity, the one whose name sorts last wins. The system must have `"shard.LocalTransform"` in its `writes` (`shard.systems`). `transform` is read now. `SHARD_E_NOT_FOUND` : the entity has no actor now (a placeholder, or an entity a plugin spawned itself) : nothing moves. An actor that is deactivated when the phase ends ignores it. thread : system

```c
ShardResult set_local_transform(ShardEcs ecs, ShardEntity entity, const ShardLocalTransform* transform);
```

**The engine's own components, found by name with `shard.components`' `find_type`**

Read them ; do not write their blocks : the actor's components are what drives them, and they overwrite what a system writes.

#### ShardActorLink

`"shard.ActorLink"` : on the entity of every actor, the actor's object id

```c
int32_t objectId;
```

`"shard.Disabled"` (1 byte, no field) : on the entity of an actor that is deactivated. Put it in `without` to skip those.

### shard_systems.h

Interface `"shard.systems"` 1.0 : functions the engine's scheduler runs every frame, in a phase, in parallel with the systems they do not conflict with (one writes what the other reads or writes). A system is named `"<plugin id>/<name>"` by the host and is removed with the plugin. A system added before the engine built its scheduler (from `on_load`) starts with the first frame.

| | Value | |
|---|---|---|
| `SHARD_IFACE_SYSTEMS` | `"shard.systems"` |  |

The phases of a frame, always run in this order. Fixed runs 0..N times per frame (as many fixed steps as the elapsed time pays for).

| | Value | |
|---|---|---|
| `SHARD_PHASE_INPUT` | `0u` |  |
| `SHARD_PHASE_PRE_SIM` | `1u` |  |
| `SHARD_PHASE_FIXED` | `2u` |  |
| `SHARD_PHASE_POST_PHYSICS` | `3u` |  |
| `SHARD_PHASE_UPDATE` | `4u` |  |
| `SHARD_PHASE_LATE` | `5u` |  |
| `SHARD_PHASE_EXTRACT` | `6u` |  |
| `SHARD_SYSTEM_EXCLUSIVE` | `1u` | touches what reads / writes cannot say : runs alone, in order |
| `SHARD_SYSTEM_MAIN_THREAD` | `2u` | needs the thread that runs the frame : the phase then runs on it, in order |

#### ShardSystemCtx

What a run of a system is given. Valid during the run only.

```c
uint32_t structSize;
float deltaTime;    // the variable step ; the fixed step in SHARD_PHASE_FIXED
float fixedDeltaTime;
int32_t fixedStep;    // SHARD_PHASE_FIXED : index of this step in the frame, from 0
int32_t fixedStepCount;    // SHARD_PHASE_FIXED : how many steps this frame runs
uint64_t frame;
ShardEcs ecs;    // for shard.ecs
```

Returns `SHARD_OK`. Any other result is counted as an error of the plugin ; at the tenth, the host fails it. thread : the system's

```c
typedef ShardResult (*ShardSystemFn)(void* user, ShardPluginCtx ctx, const ShardSystemCtx* run);
```

#### ShardSystemDesc

```c
uint32_t structSize;
uint32_t phase;    // SHARD_PHASE_*
uint32_t flags;    // SHARD_SYSTEM_*
uint32_t readCount, writeCount;
uint32_t afterCount, beforeCount;
ShardStr name;    // "rotate" : registered as "<plugin id>/rotate"
const ShardComponentType* reads;
const ShardComponentType* writes;
```

Explicit order, systems of the same phase only. A full name (`"com.acme.weather/wind"`), or `"./x"` for this plugin's `"x"`.

```c
const ShardStr* after;
const ShardStr* before;
ShardSystemFn run;
void* user;    // handed back to run
```

#### ShardSystemsApi

```c
uint32_t structSize;
```

Everything in desc is copied. `SHARD_E_ALREADY_EXISTS` : this plugin has a system of that name. thread : main

```c
ShardResult add(ShardPluginCtx ctx, const ShardSystemDesc* desc);
```

`name` as given to add. thread : main. `SHARD_E_NOT_FOUND` : no such system of this plugin.

```c
ShardResult set_enabled(ShardPluginCtx ctx, ShardStr name, int32_t enabled);
ShardResult remove(ShardPluginCtx ctx, ShardStr name);
```

### shard_events.h

Interface `"shard.events"` 1.1 : events found by NAME, carrying bytes.

The engine's C++ events are found by their C++ type, which a binary built by another compiler cannot name : the C ABI has a channel of its own, where an event is a name (`"com.acme.weather.RainStarted"`) and a payload of bytes whose layout the sender documents. C++ code reaches the same channel (`EventRegistrar::SubscribeNamed` / EmitNamed). Subscriptions end with the plugin (disable or unload).

Delivery : an event emitted on the main thread outside of the systems is delivered at once, to the subscribers in the order they subscribed. One emitted from a system (any thread) is queued and delivered on the main thread at the end of the frame, the queues of the systems taken in the order of their names : the order does not depend on which system finished first.

| | Value | |
|---|---|---|
| `SHARD_IFACE_EVENTS` | `"shard.events"` |  |

```c
typedef uint64_t ShardSubscription;    // 0 is never valid
```

`name` and `payload` are valid for the call. thread : main

```c
typedef void (*ShardEventFn)(void* user, ShardPluginCtx ctx, ShardStr name, const void* payload, uint64_t size);
```

#### ShardEventsApi

```c
uint32_t structSize;
```

Events sent globally under `name`. thread : main

```c
ShardResult subscribe(ShardPluginCtx ctx, ShardStr name, ShardEventFn fn, void* user, ShardSubscription* out);
```

Events sent to one world (its asset id) under `name`. thread : main

```c
ShardResult subscribe_world(ShardPluginCtx ctx, int32_t worldId, ShardStr name, ShardEventFn fn, void* user, ShardSubscription* out);
```

thread : main. `SHARD_E_NOT_FOUND` : not one of this plugin's live subscriptions.

```c
ShardResult unsubscribe(ShardPluginCtx ctx, ShardSubscription subscription);
```

The payload is copied. thread : any (see the delivery rules above). `SHARD_E_UNSUPPORTED` : the engine has no dispatcher (an offline tool).

```c
ShardResult emit(ShardPluginCtx ctx, ShardStr name, const void* payload, uint64_t size);
ShardResult emit_world(ShardPluginCtx ctx, int32_t worldId, ShardStr name, const void* payload, uint64_t size);
```

**1.1**

Says what the payload of the events named `name` holds, field by field (the fields of `shard_components.h`, offsets in the payload), so that the tools can show them : the console's event.watch prints each one. One description per name : `SHARD_E_ALREADY_EXISTS` if another plugin described it. It goes with the plugin. Optional : events nobody described are shown as their size. thread : main

```c
ShardResult describe(ShardPluginCtx ctx, ShardStr name, uint32_t size, const ShardFieldDesc* fields, uint32_t fieldCount);
```

### shard_hooks.h

Interface `"shard.hooks"` 1.0 : the points of the engine a plugin can intercept, and cancel. Hooks are found by name ; every one is described by the same struct, whose `subject`, `detail` and `frame` mean what the table below says. Handlers run by priority, then by plugin load order, then in the order they were added : the same order on every run. They are removed with the plugin.

```
name                 subject             detail          frame
"PreEngineInit"      -                   -               -
"PostEngineInit"     -                   -               -
"PreWorldLoad"       the world's name    -               -       cancellable : the world is not loaded
"PostWorldLoad"      the world's name    -               -
"PrePlay"            -                   -               -       cancellable : play mode does not start
"PostPlay"           -                   -               -
"PreFrame"           -                   -               frame
"PostFrame"          -                   -               frame
"PreSave"            what is saved       -               -       cancellable : nothing is saved
"AssetImported"      the asset's path    -               -
"PlayerConnecting"   the client's name   its address     -       cancellable : the client is refused, `reason` is what it is told
"PreShutdown"        -                   -               -
```

| | Value | |
|---|---|---|
| `SHARD_IFACE_HOOKS` | `"shard.hooks"` |  |
| `SHARD_PRIORITY_EARLIEST` | `(-200)` |  |
| `SHARD_PRIORITY_EARLY` | `(-100)` |  |
| `SHARD_PRIORITY_NORMAL` | `0` |  |
| `SHARD_PRIORITY_LATE` | `100` |  |
| `SHARD_PRIORITY_LATEST` | `200` |  |

```c
typedef uint64_t ShardHookToken;    // 0 is never valid
```

#### ShardHookArgs

```c
uint32_t structSize;
uint8_t cancelled;    // in : an earlier handler cancelled ; out : set it to 1 to cancel (a later handler may see it and set it back)
uint8_t reserved[3];
ShardStr name;    // the hook's name
ShardStr subject;    // see the table ; valid for the call
ShardStr detail;
uint64_t frame;
ShardStr reason;    // out : why it was cancelled, copied when the handler returns
```

thread : main

```c
typedef void (*ShardHookFn)(void* user, ShardPluginCtx ctx, ShardHookArgs* hook);
```

#### ShardHooksApi

```c
uint32_t structSize;
```

`name` from the table above (`SHARD_E_NOT_FOUND` otherwise). thread : main

```c
ShardResult on(ShardPluginCtx ctx, ShardStr name, int32_t priority, ShardHookFn fn, void* user, ShardHookToken* out);
ShardResult off(ShardPluginCtx ctx, ShardHookToken token);
```

### shard_services.h

Interface `"shard.services"` 1.0 : interfaces plugins offer each other, by name and version, without including each other's code.

A service of the C ABI is a table of function pointers that starts with `uint32_t structSize` (and, like the ABI's own tables, only grows at its end), plus a `self` the functions get back. The provider publishes the header of its table ; the users include it. The engine never calls the table : it only hands it out.

A user holds a `ShardServiceRef`, not the table : resolve it before each use. When the provider is disabled or unloaded, the ref resolves to nothing (`SHARD_E_NOT_FOUND`) instead of to a table in a library that is gone. Refs are released with the plugin that took them.

| | Value | |
|---|---|---|
| `SHARD_IFACE_SERVICES` | `"shard.services"` |  |

```c
typedef uint64_t ShardServiceRef;    // 0 is never valid
```

#### ShardService

```c
uint32_t structSize;
uint32_t major, minor;    // the version the provider offers
const void* table;    // the provider's table (its first field is its structSize)
void* self;
```

#### ShardServicesApi

```c
uint32_t structSize;
```

Offers `table` and `self` as service `name` (copied ; `table` must stay valid until the plugin is disabled). thread : main. `SHARD_E_ALREADY_EXISTS` : another plugin provides that name.

```c
ShardResult provide(ShardPluginCtx ctx, ShardStr name, uint32_t major, uint32_t minor, const void* table, void* self);
```

A ref on the service `name` if its version is in `range` (`"^1.2"`, `">=1"`, `"*"`). thread : main. `SHARD_E_NOT_FOUND` : nobody provides it, or not in that range ; `SHARD_E_INVALID_ARG` : the range does not parse.

```c
ShardResult get(ShardPluginCtx ctx, ShardStr name, ShardStr range, ShardServiceRef* out);
```

What the ref points to now (the caller sets out-&gt;structSize ; the host fills what fits). thread : any. `SHARD_E_NOT_FOUND` : its provider went away ; `SHARD_E_UNSUPPORTED` : the provider is not a plugin of the C ABI (its object is not a `ShardService`).

```c
ShardResult resolve(ShardPluginCtx ctx, ShardServiceRef ref, ShardService* out);
ShardResult release(ShardPluginCtx ctx, ShardServiceRef ref);
```

### shard_extensions.h

Interface `"shard.extensions"` 1.0 : what a plugin adds to the engine's subsystems through their extension points. The C ABI offers the points whose items are only data and functions :

```
"asset.type"       a kind of asset : file extensions the project indexes, and the loader the resource cache calls
"asset.importer"   a converter from a source format the engine does not read to files it does
```

Every item is copied by the host (strings and arrays included), named, and removed with the plugin. The functions run on the main thread.

| `SHARD_POINT_ASSET_IMPORTER` | `"asset.importer"` |  |

### shard_actors.h

Interface `"shard.actors"` 1.1 (1.0 + the fields of a component, one at a time) : the actors of a world, as a script sees them.

An actor is what a world file holds and the editor's outliner shows : a name, a pose, children, tags and components. A `ShardActor` is a handle to one (a generation and a slot, never a pointer) : it fails with `SHARD_E_STALE_HANDLE` once the actor is destroyed, and a handle of another actor never takes its place. 0 is never valid.

Where it may be called (`"thread : script"`) : from the callbacks of a script (`shard_scripts.h`), from `on_load` / `on_play_start`... and the other callbacks of the plugin that run on the main thread. NOT from a system (`shard_systems.h`) : a system runs beside others, and the actors are not made for that (`SHARD_E_WRONG_THREAD`). A system moves an actor with `shard.ecs`' `set_local_transform`.

"In the world of `anchor``" : the functions that create or look for actors work in the world the anchor actor is in. A script passes its owner. The engine's components are reached by the name their serialized form carries ("`light`", "`model"...), their fields as JSON text : the format of the world files, so anything the editor shows can be read and set from here.

| | Value | |
|---|---|---|
| `SHARD_IFACE_ACTORS` | `"shard.actors"` |  |

```c
typedef uint64_t ShardActor;    // 0 is never valid : "no actor"
```

```c

```

**Identity and state**


The name, as the `"text out"` of the ABI : at most `capacity` bytes into `buffer`, the full length in `*size`. thread : script

```c

ShardResult set_name(ShardActor actor, ShardStr name);
int32_t is_active(ShardActor actor);
ShardResult set_active(ShardActor actor, int32_t active);
```

Removes the actor, its components (their scripts get `on_destroyed`) and its children. The handle is stale afterwards.

```c

```

**Pose : `ShardLocalTransform` (`shard_ecs.h`), rotation as a quaternion x, y, z, w**

relative to the parent

in the world (the root reference frame's axes) ; the scale is the lossy one of a parent that is scaled and rotated

A new actor (with its Transform) at the root of the world of `anchor`, or under `parent` (0 : the root). `*out` is the actor.

**Components, by the name their serialized form carries (`"light"`, `"model"`, `"physics_body"`, or `"<plugin id>.<name>"`)**

Adds one. `fields_json` : the fields to set, a JSON object (`"{ \"`intensity\`": 3 }"`), or an empty string. `SHARD_E_NOT_FOUND` : unknown type.

The component as the world file writes it (a JSON object), as a `"text out"`. `SHARD_E_NOT_FOUND` : the actor has none.

**One field of a component (1.1)**

`path` is a field of the component (`"intensity"`, `"motionType"`, `"active"`) or a path into it, the names and indexes of the world file's JSON separated by '/' (`"materials/0"`, `"shapes/0/params/radius"`). A value is JSON text : 2.5, true, `"Dynamic"`, {`"x"`:0,`"y"`:1,`"z"`:0}. Assets read as their name in the project and are written as that name or as their id. `SHARD_E_NOT_FOUND` : no such component or field.

The value, as a `"text out"`

```c

```

Sets one field and nothing else : a field of the engine goes through the component's own change hook, like an edit in the inspector (a physics body keeps its velocity when its friction changes). An array grows to hold the index it is given (`"materials/2"` on one material: the gap holds 0) and `"-"` appends (`"shapes/-"`). `SHARD_E_INVALID_ARG` : the value does not fit the field.

```c
ShardResult set_component_field(ShardActor actor, ShardStr type, ShardStr path, ShardStr value_json);
```

Removes an element of an array (`"shapes/1"`) or a key of an object

```c

```

### shard_audio.h

Interface `"shard.audio"` 1.0 : sounds.

Two ways to make a sound. An actor with an `"audio"` component (add it with `shard.actors`' `add_component`, its clip, volume and 3D settings are fields of the component) is played and paused here. A one shot sound needs no actor : it plays once from a place and removes itself when it ends.

A clip is an asset of the project, named by its path in the project (`"sounds/shot.wav"`). Volumes are 1 for the clip's own level.

thread : script (`shard_actors.h` says where that is). `SHARD_E_UNSUPPORTED` : this host has no audio (an offline tool). A host that runs with no sound device (a server, the tests) accepts every call and plays nothing.

|---|---|---|
| `SHARD_IFACE_AUDIO` | `"shard.audio"` |  |

### shard_editor.h

Interface `"shard.editor"` 1.1 : the editor's windows, menus, toolbar, inspectors and gizmos, drawn with a small set of widgets.

ImGui has no stable ABI, so a plugin does not draw with it : it adds a panel and draws the contents with the widgets of `ShardUiApi`, which the editor implements with its own ImGui. The panel is a window of the editor's Window menu (hidden until the user opens it). Its draw function runs every frame while the window is open, on the editor's main thread, and may call the widgets then and only then. The same widgets draw an inspector (below a component in the Properties panel) ; `ShardGizmoApi` draws over the viewport.

This interface exists only in the editor : in the player, in headless runs and in the offline tools `query_interface` answers `SHARD_E_NOT_FOUND`, so a plugin that has panels keeps working there. The editor loads a plugin whose manifest `"hosts"` include `"engine"` (the default) or `"editor"`. A sandboxed plugin (tier 2) needs the permission `"editor"` in its manifest.

Widgets that take a value change it in place and return `SHARD_TRUE` on the frame the user changed it. A label may carry a hidden id after `"##"` (`"Speed##enemy1"`), as in ImGui, to tell apart two widgets with the same text.

1.1 added to `ShardUiApi` (from `text_disabled` on) : more text, vectors, multiline text, groups, children, disabled sections, tabs, tables, menus, popups, item queries, and to `ShardEditorApi` (from `add_menu_item` on) : menu items, toolbar buttons, inspectors, gizmos, the selection, notifications.

| | Value | |
|---|---|---|
| `SHARD_IFACE_EDITOR` | `"shard.editor"` |  |

### shard_experimental.h

Interface `"shard.experimental.world_ecs"` 0.1 : the engine's entities from the main thread, outside the systems.

The interfaces named `"shard.experimental.*"` are offered so that what may still change can be tried before it is frozen into the ABI. They carry NO compatibility promise : one may change or disappear in any revision of the engine. Their major is 0, and `query_interface` hands one out only for the exact minor the engine has (`query_interface`(`"shard.experimental.world_ecs"`, 0, 1, ...)) : a plugin built against another one does not get it. A native plugin that carries a valid signature of a trusted publisher (what is distributed) is refused them : every function returns `SHARD_E_UNSUPPORTED`. Their structs are not pinned by the layout tests.

`world_ecs` : `open()` gives a `ShardEcs` over the engine's registry that every function of `shard.ecs` (`shard_ecs.h`) accepts, as an exclusive system would (any type) ; the structural changes are applied by `close()`. Between the two, the main thread functions of the other interfaces keep working. Open and close in the same callback ; what a plugin leaves open is closed when its context goes.

| | Value | |
|---|---|---|
| `SHARD_IFACE_EXPERIMENTAL_WORLD_ECS` | `"shard.experimental.world_ecs"` |  |

#### ShardWorldEcsApi

```c
uint32_t structSize;
```

thread : main, outside the systems and while no phase runs (`SHARD_E_WRONG_THREAD`). `SHARD_E_UNSUPPORTED` : the plugin may not use experimental interfaces, or this host has no registry (an offline tool).

```c
ShardResult open(ShardPluginCtx ctx, ShardEcs* out);
```

Applies the structural changes recorded since open, in order. The last opened first.

```c
ShardResult close(ShardPluginCtx ctx, ShardEcs ecs);
```

### shard_physics.h

Interface `"shard.physics"` 1.0 : the rigid bodies of actors, and ray casts.

A body is the engine's `"physics_body"` component of an actor (add it with `shard.actors`' `add_component`, its shape and mass are fields of the component). These functions move and push the body of an actor : its handle is the actor's. Positions, directions and velocities are in the world, in the units of the project (one unit is one metre unless the project says otherwise), forces in newtons and impulses in newton seconds. Contacts are not asked for here : a script is told about them (on\_contact\_\* in `shard_scripts.h`).

thread : script (`shard_actors.h` says where that is). `SHARD_E_NOT_FOUND` : the actor has no physics body, or it has no live body yet. `SHARD_E_UNSUPPORTED` : this host has no physics (an offline tool).

| | Value | |
|---|---|---|
| `SHARD_IFACE_PHYSICS` | `"shard.physics"` |  |

The layers a ray looks at (a bit mask)

| | Value | |
|---|---|---|
| `SHARD_LAYER_STATIC` | `1u` | bodies that never move |
| `SHARD_LAYER_MOVING` | `2u` | kinematic and dynamic bodies |
| `SHARD_LAYER_ALL` | `3u` |  |

#### ShardRayHit

```c
uint32_t structSize;
ShardActor actor;    // the actor whose body the ray hit
float point[3];    // where, in the world
float normal[3];    // the surface's normal there, pointing out of the body
float distance;    // from the origin along the ray
```

#### ShardPhysicsApi

```c
uint32_t structSize;
```

Velocities, in the world

```c
ShardResult get_velocity(ShardActor actor, float out[3]);
ShardResult set_velocity(ShardActor actor, const float velocity[3]);
ShardResult get_angular_velocity(ShardActor actor, float out[3]);
ShardResult set_angular_velocity(ShardActor actor, const float velocity[3]);
```

A force acts for the step it is added in (call it every step to push for longer), an impulse changes the velocity at once. A point is in the world : a force or impulse off the centre of mass also turns the body.

```c
ShardResult add_force(ShardActor actor, const float force[3]);
ShardResult add_force_at_point(ShardActor actor, const float force[3], const float point[3]);
ShardResult add_torque(ShardActor actor, const float torque[3]);
ShardResult add_impulse(ShardActor actor, const float impulse[3]);
ShardResult add_impulse_at_point(ShardActor actor, const float impulse[3], const float point[3]);
ShardResult add_angular_impulse(ShardActor actor, const float impulse[3]);
```

The acceleration the body falls with now, from the world's gravity and the gravity fields where it is (or its own custom gravity)

```c
ShardResult get_gravity(ShardActor actor, float out[3]);
```

Gives the body a gravity of its own : the world's gravity and the fields no longer reach it

```c
ShardResult set_custom_gravity(ShardActor actor, const float gravity[3]);
```

The first body a ray meets. `direction` need not be normalized (a zero one is `SHARD_E_INVALID_ARG`). `layers` : `SHARD_LAYER_*`. `ignore` : an actor whose body the ray goes through (the one that fires it), or 0. `SHARD_OK` and `*out` filled when something is hit, `SHARD_E_NOT_FOUND` when nothing is within `max_distance`.

```c
ShardResult raycast(const float origin[3], const float direction[3], float max_distance, uint32_t layers, ShardActor ignore, ShardRayHit* out);
```

### shard_scripts.h

Interface `"shard.scripts"` 1.1 : scripts, the components that carry a plugin's gameplay code.

A script is an object of the plugin (a C++ class in the SDK) that lives on an actor, as the engine's own Script components do. The host owns its memory and calls it back : it is created with the component, receives the callbacks of the actor's life and of the frame (play, tick, fixed tick, late tick, stop...), in the order of the scripts of the world, and goes with the actor. Its fields are shown by the inspector, saved with the world and copied with the actor (play mode copies the world), exactly as for a component of `shard_components.h` : the same `ShardFieldDesc`, the same field types (text, assets, blobs included), at offsets in the object.

Unlike a component's block, the object is NOT plain data : it is constructed in place in storage the host provides (`size` bytes, aligned on `align`), and destructed there. It is never moved or copied by the host with memcpy. A copy of the actor (play mode) constructs a new object and copies the described fields into it : what is not a field starts fresh, as if the actor was just created.

Threads : every callback runs on the thread that ticks the scripts of the world, one script after the other, never two at once : what a script does with `shard_actors.h` and `shard_input.h` is safe there. The functions of this table are `"thread : main"` (from `on_load`).

| | Value | |
|---|---|---|
| `SHARD_IFACE_SCRIPTS` | `"shard.scripts"` |  |
| `SHARD_SCRIPT_MAX_SIZE` | `16384u` | bytes of an object |

The callbacks of a script. All are optional but construct and destruct. A callback returns `SHARD_OK`, or an error that the host logs and counts as an error of the plugin (at the tenth the host fails the plugin, as for a system). `object` is what construct built.

```c
typedef ShardResult (*ShardScriptFn)(void* user, void* object);
typedef ShardResult (*ShardScriptTickFn)(void* user, void* object, float delta_time);
```

#### ShardContact

What a script is told about a contact of its actor's body with another one (physics, ABI 1.5). `other` is the other body's actor. `normal` points from this actor toward the other one. `point` is a point of the contact in the world, `penetration` how deep the bodies overlap. `on_contact_ended` only fills `other`.

```c
uint32_t structSize;
ShardActor other;
float point[3];
float normal[3];
float penetration;
```

```c
typedef ShardResult (*ShardScriptContactFn)(void* user, void* object, const ShardContact* contact);
```

#### ShardScriptCallbacks

```c
uint32_t structSize;
```

Builds the object in `storage` : fields at their defaults, no actor yet. Called when the component is made (an actor getting it, the world file read, a copy of an actor). `SHARD_OK`, or an error to refuse (the component is not made).

```c
ShardResult construct(void* user, void* storage);
```

Destroys the object. The storage is the host's to free.

```c
void destruct(void* user, void* storage);
```

The component joined an actor : this is its owner, valid as long as the object lives. Called once, before `on_create`.

```c
ShardResult attach(void* user, void* object, ShardActor owner);
ShardScriptFn on_create;    // the script joined an actor that is in a world (Script::OnCreate)
ShardScriptFn on_world_loaded;    // the world finished loading (for actors tagged "Persistent")
ShardScriptFn on_world_unloaded;
ShardScriptFn on_play;    // play mode starts
ShardScriptTickFn on_tick;    // every frame, in the Update phase : delta_time is the frame's
ShardScriptTickFn on_fixed_tick;    // every fixed step, right before the physics step : delta_time is the step's
ShardScriptTickFn on_late_tick;    // every frame, after the scripts and the physics moved everything
ShardScriptFn on_stop;    // play mode stops
ShardScriptFn on_destroyed;    // the component or its actor is destroyed, before destruct
ShardScriptFn on_activated;
ShardScriptFn on_deactivated;
```

1.5 : physics contacts, in the physics step's callbacks, on the thread that steps the physics

```c
ShardScriptContactFn on_contact_added;
ShardScriptContactFn on_contact_persisted;
ShardScriptContactFn on_contact_ended;
```

1.5 : the plugin's own strings. A field `SHARD_FIELD_STRING` with `SHARD_FIELD_ACCESSOR` is the object's `std::string` (or any string of the plugin's) at that offset : the host never reads its memory, it asks these. `text_get` gives the text (valid until the next call into the object), `text_set` replaces it. Both are required when a field has the flag.

```c
void text_get(void* user, void* object, uint32_t offset, ShardStr* out);
ShardResult text_set(void* user, void* object, uint32_t offset, ShardStr text);
```

Callbacks of later ABI revisions go HERE : the host checks structSize before reading them.

#### ShardScriptDesc

```c
uint32_t structSize;
uint32_t size;    // bytes of the object, 1 to SHARD_SCRIPT_MAX_SIZE
uint32_t align;    // a power of two, 16 at most
uint32_t fieldCount;    // SHARD_COMPONENT_MAX_FIELDS at most
ShardStr name;    // "Health" : the host registers "<plugin id>.Health", the name a world file calls it
const ShardFieldDesc* fields;    // offsets in the object. Read during the call only.
void* user;    // handed back to every callback
const ShardScriptCallbacks* callbacks;    // copied up to its structSize during the call
```

#### ShardScriptsApi

```c
uint32_t structSize;
```

Registers a script type, from `on_load`. thread : main. `SHARD_E_INVALID_ARG` : a field out of the object, misaligned or overlapping another, a bad name, a size or an alignment out of bounds, no construct or destruct (the log says which). `SHARD_E_ALREADY_EXISTS` : the name is taken.

```c
ShardResult register_script(ShardPluginCtx ctx, const ShardScriptDesc* desc);
```

The object of the script `name` (as registered, `"Health"`) that `actor` has, if it belongs to this plugin : NULL in `*out` otherwise. Valid until the script is removed or the actor destroyed. thread : script

```c
ShardResult get_object(ShardPluginCtx ctx, ShardActor actor, ShardStr name, void** out);
```

Adds the script `name` to `actor` and returns its object. A script of this plugin only. thread : script

```c
ShardResult add_to_actor(ShardPluginCtx ctx, ShardActor actor, ShardStr name, void** out);
```

### shard_wasm.h

Sandboxed plugins (tier 2, `"abi"`: `"wasm1"`) : the C ABI, for a module built for wasm32 (`docs/design-notes/wasm-sandbox.fr.md`). Experimental : it is not covered by the ABI's compatibility promise yet.

A sandboxed plugin is the plugin you would write for the C ABI (`shard.h`, or `shard/game.hpp` in C++), compiled to WebAssembly. It can touch nothing but its own memory and what the host gives it : no files, no network, no clock, no randomness of the system. It loads without a signature or a consent, because it cannot do more than the host lets it : the interfaces below, filtered by the `"permissions"` of its manifest. Its time (budgets.frameMs per frame) and its memory (budgets.memoryMB) are bounded ; a trap (a division by zero, an access out of its memory, an `unreachable`), an exhausted budget or an import used wrongly stops the plugin, never the engine.

The same source compiles for the engine and for wasm32. This header is all it takes : including it (`shard.h` does, when compiling for wasm) declares every function of the interfaces as an import of the host and builds the tables (`ShardCVarsApi`...) from them. The `ShardHostApi` that `shard_plugin_entry` receives is `shard_wasm_host_table`, which the module exports ; `query_interface` answers from the module's tables. See `shard_wasm_imports.h` (generated from the other headers) for the list.

What differs from a native plugin :

* the interfaces : `shard.plugin`, commands, cvars, components, ecs, systems, events, state, scripts, actors, input, physics, audio, worlds,
```
and shard.content for the plugin's own folder ("fs.read:content"). Not offered : shard.editor, hooks, services, extensions, experimental.
```

* permissions : `shard.content` needs `"fs.read:content"`, `shard.input` `"input"`, `shard.physics` `"physics"`, `shard.audio` `"audio"` (without it
```
query_interface says SHARD_E_NOT_FOUND and the functions answer SHARD_E_UNSUPPORTED, or SHARD_FALSE / 0), worlds.load_world
"worlds.load", actors.create / actors.spawn / worlds.spawn_prefab "actors.spawn".
```

* memory of the host is copied : the block of a component that `shard.ecs` hands out, the bytes of a blob and the object of a script
```
live in the module, and what the module changed is copied back when the call that made the copy returns (a system, a script's
callback, a command...). A blob's pointer stays valid until the module resizes or frees the blob. A string the host hands out
(shard.components string_get) is valid until the call returns.
```

* the systems of a module run on the main thread, one after the other : a module is never entered by two threads at once.
* `ShardPluginCtx` : whatever a module passes, an import acts for the plugin the module belongs to.
* `shard.content.read` gives memory that is freed with `ShardHostApi::free` ; resolve and `resolve_logical` (which would give a path of the
```
host) are always SHARD_E_UNSUPPORTED, and read / list only reach the plugin's own mod:// address.
```

* the host's alloc and free are the module's memory (they count against budgets.memoryMB).

Building one, in C without a libc :

```
clang --target=wasm32 -ffreestanding -nostdlib -O2 -I<sdk>/include -c plugin.c -o plugin.o
wasm-ld --no-entry --export=shard_plugin_entry --export=shard_wasm_host_table --export-table -o plugin.wasm plugin.o
```

... and in C++ with wasi-sdk (a libc and a libc++ for wasm32, no exceptions) :

```
clang++ --target=wasm32-wasi -fno-exceptions -DSHARD_SDK_NO_EXCEPTIONS -O2 -I<sdk>/include -c a.cpp b.cpp
wasm-ld ... or clang++ -mexec-model=reactor -Wl,--export=shard_plugin_entry -Wl,--export=shard_wasm_host_table -Wl,--export-table
```

`shard_sdk_add_plugin`(... TARGET wasm) does that (`sdk/cmake/ShardSDKPlugin.cmake`). The module must export its memory (`"memory"`, wasm-ld's default) and its function table (`"__indirect_function_table"`, --export-table) : the host reads the arguments of the imports in the first and calls the callbacks through the second. A module with C++ constructors (or a libc to start) exports `_initialize` (wasi-sdk reactors do) or `__wasm_call_ctors` : the host runs it before the entry point. The module's allocator must get its memory from memory.grow, as wasi-libc's does : the host adds pages of its own after the module's.

### shard_worlds.h

Interface `"shard.worlds"` 1.0 : loading worlds, and prefabs.

A world is loaded by its path in the project (`"worlds/arena.world"`). The load is a request : it starts in the background, and the world is swapped in at the start of a following frame, where the old worlds are unloaded (their scripts get `on_destroyed`) and the new one is loaded (the plugin's `on_world_loaded` is called). A script that asks for a load keeps running until then, so nothing it holds is pulled from under it in the middle of a frame.

A prefab is an actor stored as JSON in the content of a module (`prefabs/<name>.json`, `shard_content.h`) : the form the editor writes an actor in. Spawning one builds the actor, its components and its children.

thread : script (`shard_actors.h` says where that is).

| | Value | |
|---|---|---|
| `SHARD_IFACE_WORLDS` | `"shard.worlds"` |  |

#### ShardWorldsApi

```c
uint32_t structSize;
```

Asks for that world to replace the loaded ones. `SHARD_E_NOT_FOUND` : the project has no such world. `SHARD_E_ALREADY_EXISTS` : a load is already under way (ask again once `is_loading` says it is over). `SHARD_E_UNSUPPORTED` : this host has no worlds.

```c
ShardResult load_world(ShardStr path_in_project);
```

`SHARD_TRUE` while a requested load is under way.

```c
int32_t is_loading(void);
```

How many worlds are loaded.

```c
int32_t loaded_count(void);
```

Builds the prefab in the world of `anchor`, under `parent` (0 : at the root), and returns its actor. `prefab` is a `mod://` address (`"mod://com.acme.game/prefabs/crate.json"`), a logical path (`"prefabs/crate.json"`), or a bare name (`"crate"`, read as `"prefabs/crate.json"`). `SHARD_E_NOT_FOUND` : no such file. `SHARD_E_INVALID_ARG` : it is not an actor.

```c
ShardResult spawn_prefab(ShardActor anchor, ShardStr prefab, ShardActor parent, ShardActor* out);
```

## The C++ SDK

`sdk/include/shard/cpp` : header-only C++17 over the C ABI, compiled into the plugin. `#include <shard/cpp/plugin.hpp>` brings all of it. Every callback of the SDK catches what the plugin throws : `Shard::Error` (what a registration the host refused throws, with its `ShardResult`) and anything else become an error of that callback, with the message in the log. Below, the public declarations of each header (bodies left out).

### shard/cpp/plugin.hpp

Shard C++ SDK : a plugin class over the C ABI.

```cpp
class SpinPlugin : public Shard::Plugin {
public:
    void OnLoad(Shard::Context& ctx) override { ... }
};
SHARD_C_PLUGIN(SpinPlugin)
```

The macro exports `shard_plugin_entry` and fills the callbacks table : every callback catches what the plugin throws (`Shard::Error` from a refused registration, or anything else) and turns it into an error the host fails the plugin with, the message in its log. Nothing of the engine is included or linked : this compiles against `sdk/include` alone, with any C++17 compiler.

#### `Context`

What the host knows of the plugin, and every way the plugin reaches it

```cpp
ShardPluginCtx Handle() const;
std::string_view Id() const;
std::string_view Version() const;
/// The plugin's folder, absolute
std::string_view Directory() const;
/// "editor", "player", "headless" or "tool" (empty in an engine of ABI 1.0)
std::string_view HostName() const;
/// True if the manifest asks for that permission (false in an engine of ABI 1.0)
bool HasPermission(std::string_view permission) const;
void Log(std::string_view message) const;
void Warn(std::string_view message) const;
void Error(std::string_view message) const;
/// Memory counted against the plugin's budget (manifest budgets.memoryMB) : give it back with Free
void* Alloc(size_t size, size_t align = 16) const;
void Free(void* p) const;
Shard::Components Components() const;
Shard::Systems Systems() const;
Shard::Scripts Scripts() const;
Shard::Editor Editor() const;
Shard::CVars CVars() const;
Shard::Commands Commands() const;
Shard::Events Events() const;
Shard::Hooks Hooks() const;
Shard::Services Services() const;
Shard::Content Content() const;
Shard::Extensions Extensions() const;
```

#### `World`

A world a module is told about

```cpp
int32_t assetId = -1;
std::string_view name;
```

#### `Plugin`

The base of a plugin written with the SDK : the same calls, in the same order, as the engine's IPlugin (see `shard_host.h`)

```cpp
/// Register everything here (components, systems, cvars, commands, services, hooks...)
virtual void OnLoad(Context&);
/// Every plugin ran OnLoad : the services of the others can be asked for
virtual void OnInitialize(Context&);
virtual void OnEnable(Context&);
virtual void OnDisable(Context&);
virtual void OnUnload(Context&);
/// Hot reload : write what must survive and return true ; false (the default) makes the plugin not reloadable
virtual bool OnPrepareReload(Context&, StateWriter&);
virtual void OnRestore(Context&, StateReader&);
virtual void OnFrameBegin(Context&, uint64_t /*frame*/);
virtual void OnFrameEnd(Context&, uint64_t /*frame*/);
virtual void OnContentMounted(Context&);
virtual void OnWorldLoaded(Context&, const World&);
virtual void OnWorldUnloaded(Context&, const World&);
virtual void OnPlayStart(Context&, const World&);
virtual void OnPlayStop(Context&, const World&);
/// An offline tool is about to run `task` ("cook", "bake", "validate") : return false (and a message) to cancel it
virtual bool OnToolTask(Context&, std::string_view /*task*/, std::string_view /*project*/, std::string& /*message*/);
```

```cpp
/// Exports the entry point of the C ABI for a class derived from Shard::Plugin (once per plugin, in one source file)
SHARD_C_PLUGIN(ClassName)
/// A plugin that is only what its source files register (scripts, components, systems: shard/cpp/registry.hpp): the entry point, in any one of them
SHARD_GAME_MODULE()
```

### shard/cpp/component.hpp

Shard C++ SDK : component types from C++ structs.

```cpp
struct Spin { float speed = 1.f; float angle = 0.f; Shard::Vec3 axis{ 0.f, 1.f, 0.f }; };
SHARD_COMPONENT(Spin, (speed)(angle)(axis))
```

(at global scope) declares which members are fields (their type and offset are deduced) ; the struct's default member values are the defaults of a new component. The struct must be trivially copyable and standard layout : it is the block the engine copies with memcpy (`shard_components.h`). Register it in OnLoad with `ctx.Components().Register<Spin>("Spin")`.

#### `Vec2`

```cpp
float x = 0.f, y = 0.f;
```

#### `Vec3`

```cpp
float x = 0.f, y = 0.f, z = 0.f;
```

#### `Vec4`

```cpp
float x = 0.f, y = 0.f, z = 0.f, w = 0.f;
```

#### `Quat`

```cpp
float x = 0.f, y = 0.f, z = 0.f, w = 1.f;
```

#### `Color`

```cpp
float r = 1.f, g = 1.f, b = 1.f, a = 1.f;
```

#### `FieldType<float>, FieldType<double>, FieldType<int32_t>, FieldType<uint32_t>, FieldType<int64_t>, FieldType<uint64_t>, FieldType<bool>, FieldType<Vec2>, FieldType<Vec3>, FieldType<Vec4>, FieldType<Quat>, FieldType<Color>, FieldType<float[2]>, FieldType<float[3]>, FieldType<float[4]>, FieldType<Blob>, FieldType<std::string>, FieldType<Text>, FieldType<AssetId>`

The `SHARD_FIELD_*` of a member type. Specialize it for a type of your own with the same layout (`glm::vec3` -&gt; `SHARD_FIELD_VEC3`).

```cpp
static constexpr uint32_t value = 0;
```

#### `Blob`

A blob of this plugin (`shard_components.h`, 1.1) : bytes the host keeps outside a component's block, as many as needed. A component holds one in a member of this type ; `Components::CreateBlob` makes it. Copying the struct copies the handle, not the bytes.

```cpp
ShardBlob handle = 0;
explicit operator bool() const;
```

#### `FieldFlags`

Flags a member type adds to its field : none, except for a `std::string` of a script, which the host reads through the script's callbacks

```cpp
static constexpr uint32_t value = 0;
```

#### `Text`

A text of a component (`shard_components.h`, 1.2) : a field of this type holds a handle, the text lives in the host. The inspector shows it as a text box and the world file saves it as a string. Read it with `Components::GetText`, write it with `Components::SetText`. Copying the struct copies the handle, not the text.

```cpp
ShardBlob handle = 0;
/// The text (empty if there is none yet). thread : any
std::string Get() const;
/// Replaces the text. Throws Shard::Error over the memory budget, or in an engine older than ABI 1.3. thread : any
void Set(std::string_view text);
Text& operator=(std::string_view text);
Text& operator=(const char* text);
Text& operator=(const std::string& text);
Text& operator=(const Text&) = default;
```

#### `AssetId`

The id of an asset of the project (`shard_components.h`, 1.2), 0 for none : the inspector shows an asset picker

```cpp
int32_t id = 0;
explicit operator bool() const;
```

#### `FieldOptions`

How a field shows in the editor and whether it is saved (see `shard_components.h`)

```cpp
/// the member's name, as written in SHARD_COMPONENT
std::string name;
/// SHARD_FIELD_RUNTIME, SHARD_FIELD_PRIVATE
uint32_t flags = 0;
float min = 0.f, max = 0.f;
std::string tooltip;
/// Only the name is required : { "speed", 0, 0.f, 100.f }, { "frames", SHARD_FIELD_RUNTIME }
FieldOptions(std::string fieldName, uint32_t fieldFlags = 0, float lowest = 0.f, float highest = 0.f, std::string hint = {}) : name(std::move(fieldName)), flags(fieldFlags), min(lowest), max(highest), tooltip(std::move(hint));
```

#### `FieldList`

The fields of T, filled by the specialization `SHARD_COMPONENT` writes

```cpp
template <typename M> void Add(const char* name, M T::* member);
const std::vector<Entry>& Entries() const;
```

#### `ComponentTraits`

Which members of T are fields : `SHARD_COMPONENT` specializes it

```cpp
static constexpr bool kDescribed = false;
```

#### `ComponentType`

A component type the host knows, typed : what queries and systems take

```cpp
ShardComponentType handle = 0;
explicit operator bool() const;
```

```cpp
/// A type of the engine or of another plugin, whose layout the caller knows (shard_ecs.h documents the engine's)
template <typename T> ComponentType<T> AsComponentType(ShardComponentType handle);
```

#### `Components`

```cpp
/// Registers T as "<plugin id>.<name>" (from OnLoad). Throws Shard::Error if the host refuses it (the log says why).
template <typename T> ComponentType<T> Register(const std::string& name, std::initializer_list<FieldOptions> options = {});
/// A blob of `size` bytes, zeroed. Throws Shard::Error over the memory budget, or in an engine older than ABI 1.2. thread : any
Blob CreateBlob(uint64_t size) const;
/// Its bytes (null if the blob is not one of this plugin's) ; valid until it is resized or freed. thread : any
void* BlobData(Blob blob, uint64_t* size = nullptr) const;
bool ResizeBlob(Blob blob, uint64_t size) const;
bool FreeBlob(Blob blob) const;
/// Sets a string field of a component : `field` is the member itself (in the block of an entity, or in a copy). Throws Shard::Error over
/// the memory budget, or in an engine older than ABI 1.3. thread : any
void SetText(Text& field, std::string_view text) const;
/// The text of a string field (empty if it holds none). thread : any
```

### shard/cpp/system.hpp

Shard C++ SDK : systems and what they see of the entities.

```cpp
ctx.Systems().Add("rotate", Shard::Phase::Update)
    .Writes(spin)
    .Run([spin](Shard::SystemCtx& s) {
        s.Each(spin, [&](Spin& c) { c.angle += c.speed * s.DeltaTime(); });
    });
```

A system reads and writes only the types it declared (Reads / Writes) : the scheduler runs systems in parallel on that promise.

```cpp
using Entity = ShardEntity;
enum class Phase : uint32_t { Input = SHARD_PHASE_INPUT, PreSim = SHARD_PHASE_PRE_SIM, Fixed = SHARD_PHASE_FIXED, PostPhysics = SHARD_PHASE_POST_PHYSICS, Update = SHARD_PHASE_UPDATE, Late = SHARD_PHASE_LATE, Extract = SHARD_PHASE_EXTRACT, };
```

### shard/cpp/services.hpp

Shard C++ SDK : services between plugins (`shard_services.h`). A service is a C table of function pointers that starts with `uint32_t structSize`, published in a header by its provider :

```cpp
struct WeatherApi { uint32_t structSize; float (SHARD_CALL *rain)(void* self, float x, float z); };
ctx.Services().Provide("weather.query", 1, 0, &kWeatherApi, this);                 // the provider
auto weather = ctx.Services().Get<WeatherApi>("weather.query", "^1");              // a user, in OnInitialize
if (auto w = weather.Resolve()) w.table->rain(w.self, 0.f, 0.f);                   // before each use
```

#### `Resolved`

A service resolved now : its table and the provider's `self`. Do not keep it : resolve again before each use.

```cpp
const Table* table = nullptr;
void* self = nullptr;
uint32_t major = 0, minor = 0;
explicit operator bool() const;
```

#### `Service`

A handle on a service : empty once its provider is disabled or unloaded

```cpp
Resolved<Table> Resolve() const;
explicit operator bool() const;
```

```cpp
/// Empty if nobody provides it in that range ("^1.2", ">=1", "*")
template <typename Table> Service<Table> Get(const std::string& name, const std::string& range = "*") const;
```

### shard/cpp/actor.hpp

Shard C++ SDK : actors, the things a world holds (`shard_actors.h`).

```cpp
Shard::Actor enemy = scene.Spawn(R"({ "name": "Enemy", "components": [] })");
enemy.SetPosition({ 0.f, 1.f, -5.f });
enemy.AddTag("Enemy");
if (Health* health = enemy.GetScript<Health>()) health->Damage(10.f);
```

An Actor is a handle: copying it is free, and it stays safe when the actor is destroyed (`IsValid()` turns false, the getters return zeroes, the setters do nothing). Use it from the callbacks of a script (`Shard::Script`) : not from a system, which runs beside others.

#### `Scene`

The world an actor is in: where to create, spawn and find other actors

```cpp

/// ("prefabs/crate.json") or a bare name ("crate"). Throws Shard::Error if there is no such prefab.
```


### shard/cpp/editor.hpp

Shard C++ SDK : windows of the editor (`shard_editor.h`).

```cpp
SHARD_EDITOR_PANEL(Spawner, "Enemy spawner", ui)
{
    static int count = 5;
    ui.SliderInt("Count", count, 1, 50);
    if (ui.Button("Spawn")) SpawnEnemies(count);
}
```

The panel appears in the editor's Window menu. Menu items (`SHARD_EDITOR_MENU_ITEM`), toolbar buttons, inspectors below a component, gizmos in the viewport and the selection are in the same header. In the player, in headless runs and in the offline tools there is no editor : the panel is not added and nothing else changes, so the same plugin runs everywhere. A plugin whose manifest hosts include `"engine"` is loaded by the editor ; `"editor"` alone limits it to the editor.

### shard/cpp/engine_components.hpp

Shard C++ SDK : the engine's own components (model, light, physics body...) as typed handles, over `shard.actors`' field functions.

```cpp
Shard::Actor bullet = GetScene().Create("Bullet");

auto model = bullet.Add<Shard::Model>();
model.SetMesh(mesh);                                       // an AssetId (a field of the script), or the asset's name in the project
model.SetMaterial(0, material);

auto body = bullet.Add<Shard::PhysicsBody>();
body.SetShape(Shard::Shape::Capsule(0.1f, 0.3f));
body.SetMotionType(Shard::MotionType::Dynamic);            // the body of the new kind exists at once : the velocity has something to push
body.SetFriction(0.8f);
bullet.SetVelocity(forward * 30.f);

if (auto light = bullet.Get<Shard::Light>()) light.SetIntensity(3.f);
```

A handle is a pair (actor, component type) : copying it is free, and it stays safe when the actor goes. Every setter changes that one field and nothing else, the way an edit in the inspector does (the component's own change hook runs : a body keeps its velocity when its friction changes) and throws `Shard::Error` when the engine refuses it. The getters return a zero when the component or the field is gone.

Not every component has a class here : `Shard::ComponentRef` reaches any field of any component of the engine by its name (the one the inspector and the world file use) :

```cpp
Shard::ComponentRef probe(actor, "probeVolume");
probe.SetFloat("blendDistance", 2.f);
```

Assets read as their name in the project (the way a world file stores them) and are set from an AssetId or from that name.

```cpp
/// An enum of the engine's components, as the names the inspector shows
enum class MotionType { Static, Kinematic, Dynamic };
enum class GravityMode { Fields, World, Custom };
enum class LightType { Directional, Point, Spot };
enum class BakeMode { Dynamic, Stationary, Static };
enum class BillboardFacing { Camera, AxisY, Fixed };
```

#### `ComponentRef`

One component of an actor, reached by the names of its fields. The classes below (Model, PhysicsBody...) are this with the names written for you ; use it directly for a component that has no class here.

```cpp
/// `type` is the name the world file gives the component ("light", "physics_body", or "<plugin id>.<script>"). It must outlive the handle
/// (a literal).
ComponentRef(Actor actor, const char* type) : m_Actor(actor), m_Type(type);
const Actor& Owner() const;
const char* Type() const;
/// The actor is alive and still has the component
bool IsValid() const;
explicit operator bool() const;
/// Removes the component from its actor
bool Remove() const;
/// A deactivated component does nothing, as if it were not there
bool IsActive() const;
void SetActive(bool active) const;
/// The value as JSON text ; empty if the component or the field is not there
std::string GetJson(std::string_view path) const;
/// Sets the field to a value written as JSON text. Throws Shard::Error.
void SetJson(std::string_view path, std::string_view valueJson) const;
/// Removes an element of an array field (path "shapes/1") or a key of an object. Throws Shard::Error.
void Erase(std::string_view path) const;
void SetFloat(std::string_view path, float value) const;
void SetInt(std::string_view path, int64_t value) const;
void SetBool(std::string_view path, bool value) const;
void SetString(std::string_view path, std::string_view value) const;
void SetVec3(std::string_view path, Vec3 v) const;
void SetColor(std::string_view path, Color c) const;
/// An asset, by its id (0 : none) or by its name in the project
void SetAsset(std::string_view path, AssetId asset) const;
void SetAsset(std::string_view path, std::string_view assetName) const;
/// An enum, by the name the inspector shows ("Dynamic")
void SetEnum(std::string_view path, std::string_view name) const;
float GetFloat(std::string_view path, float fallback = 0.f) const;
int64_t GetInt(std::string_view path, int64_t fallback = 0) const;
bool GetBool(std::string_view path, bool fallback = false) const;
std::string GetString(std::string_view path) const;
Vec3 GetVec3(std::string_view path) const;
Color GetColor(std::string_view path) const;
/// The name in the project of an asset field ; empty for none
std::string GetAsset(std::string_view path) const;
/// The name of the value of an enum field ("Dynamic")
std::string GetEnum(std::string_view path) const;
/// How many elements an array field holds
size_t Count(std::string_view path) const;
```

### shard/cpp/field.hpp

Shard C++ SDK : the fields of a script, declared where the member is.

```cpp
class Gun : public Shard::Script {
public:
    SHARD_FIELD(float, power, Range(0.f, 1000.f), Tooltip("Speed of the bullet")) = 30.f;
    SHARD_FIELD(float, lifetime, Range(0.f, 60.f)) = 3.f;
    SHARD_FIELD(Shard::AssetId, mesh, Tooltip("The mesh to shoot"));
    SHARD_FIELD(int, ammo, Runtime()) = 12;                  // shown by the inspector, not saved
    float cooldown = 0.f;                                    // not a field : it stays out of the inspector and the world file
};

// gun.cpp
SHARD_REGISTER_SCRIPT(Gun)
```

The macro declares the member (`Type name`, so the default value goes after it, as for any member) and, in front of it, a one byte member that tells the SDK its name, its type, where it is in the object and its options. Nothing else lists the field : no sequence in the .cpp, no generated file. Options are the names below, written bare inside the macro:

```cpp
Range(min, max)     the bounds of the inspector's widget
Tooltip("text")     what the inspector shows when the mouse rests on the field
Runtime()           the inspector shows it, read only, and the world file does not save it
Hidden()            neither shown nor saved (the object keeps it; not for a string)
```

The type is any of the field types of `shard/cpp/component.hpp` (numbers, bool, `Vec2/3/4`, Quat, Color, Text, AssetId, `std::string`, Actor, Blob).

#### `FieldSpec`

What the options of a field add to it

```cpp
uint32_t flags = 0;
float min = 0.f, max = 0.f;
std::string tooltip;
```

#### `Range`

```cpp
float min, max;
void Apply(FieldSpec& spec) const;
```

#### `Tooltip`

```cpp
const char* text;
void Apply(FieldSpec& spec) const;
```

#### `Runtime`

```cpp
void Apply(FieldSpec& spec) const;
```

#### `Hidden`

```cpp
void Apply(FieldSpec& spec) const;
```

#### `End`

`SHARD_FIELD` ends its options with it, so that the macro never has an empty `"..."` (an error in C++17 with -pedantic)

```cpp
void Apply(FieldSpec&) const;
```

```cpp
template <typename... Options> FieldSpec MakeFieldSpec(const Options&... options);
/// Declares a field of a script : `SHARD_FIELD(float, power, Range(0.f, 1000.f)) = 30.f;` (options are optional, see the top of this file)
SHARD_FIELD(...)
```

### shard/cpp/input.hpp

Shard C++ SDK : keyboard, mouse and gamepads (`shard_input.h`).

```cpp
if (Shard::Input::IsKeyDown(Shard::Key::W)) owner.Translate(owner.Forward() * speed * dt);
const float turn = Shard::Input::Axis(Shard::Key::A, Shard::Key::D);                 // -1, 0 or 1
if (Shard::Input::WasPressed(Shard::Key::Space)) Jump();
```

What the engine's input manager sees this frame, which is also what a replay records. Call it from the callbacks of a script.

